clue.text: Like the poet's pool (or his brow ?)

definitions.text: Like the poet's pool (or his brow ?)

parts.words: Like the poet's pool (or his brow ?)
parts.note: Tennyson's Maud has a pool edged with ferns and reeds, and a brow can carry a cut of hair falling over the forehead; both are bordered

explanation.surface: A question of how a poet would describe a pond, with a teasing aside about his hairline.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson writes of a 'fringed pool' in Maud; a fringe is also the hair cut straight across the brow, so one word fits both pool and brow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool with a border of plants and a forehead with a hair bang are both edged, so both take this adjective.

clue.text: A character to reckon with

parts.note: a character can be a written symbol, and the digits are the symbols used when doing sums; the phrase also suggests a formidable person

explanation.surface: Someone formidable whom others must take seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a character to reckon with' suggests a formidable person, but a figure is a numeral, the character used in reckoning (calculating).
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a written symbol used in calculation, so it is literally a character you count with.

clue.text: No movement can retain one so reformed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: reformed means re-shaped, so the letters of the words before are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint that a stagnant organisation cannot be kept if it is reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so reformed' rearranges RETAIN plus I (one) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a state of rest or inactivity, the absence of motion.

clue.text: Poet whose output was precious?

definitions.meaning: Oliver ..., the Irish poet and playwright of The Deserted Village
a worker in gold makes things of precious metal

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote poems; a craftsman in gold produces precious objects, so the name serves both readings.

clue.text: Stick to water, perhaps

parts.note: read not as 'adhere to water' but as a stick that leads you to water, used by dowsers to find underground springs

explanation.surface: Advice to keep to water, maybe instead of something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick to' looks like a verb meaning keep to; it is a noun, a stick that leads to water, the forked twig a dowser uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsers walk with a forked twig that twitches over underground springs, so it is a stick for finding water.

clue.text: Revision courses for the very rich

definitions.note: here meaning a man of great wealth, singular, as the answer is one person

indicators.note: a revision re-works what was there, so the letters of the next word are re-arranged

explanation.surface: Crammer classes sold to wealthy students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revision' looks like exam preparation; it is the signal to rearrange COURSES. The ancient king of Lydia was proverbially wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lydian king's name became a byword for a man of enormous wealth.

clue.text: Top of a humble dwelling is all the poet uses

definitions.text: Top of a humble dwelling is all the poet uses

parts.words: Top of a humble dwelling is all the poet uses
parts.note: the first part of the word for a small country house is a short form poets use for such a home

explanation.surface: Poets refer to a humble home by only the front part of its name.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'uses'. A poet writes the short form 'cot' for a cottage, which is only the first part (top) of the word for a humble dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic diction uses this short word for a small rustic house, being the first syllable of the full word.

clue.text: Game to merit honour, be about right

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour, is abbreviated OM

indicators.note: about means around, so the word be is placed around the next piece

explanation.surface: A call to deserve a decoration by behaving properly.
explanation.walkthrough: OM, the Order of Merit, then BE placed 'about' R for right. Ombre is an old three-handed card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is a seventeenth-century card game played with forty cards.

clue.text: Strain of the point-to point ?

definitions.meaning: to strain is to pull tight or overexert
a distance between one point and another, as on a racecourse; a point-to-point is a British amateur horse race across country

explanation.definitionFit: Straining a muscle means pulling it too far, and a length of course from one mark to the next is a section of track.

clue.text: Serpent, snake; ship, vessel, for example

definitions.text: Serpent, snake; ship, vessel, for example

parts.words: Serpent, snake; ship, vessel, for example
parts.note: each pair of words means the same thing, so the pairs are instances of words with matching meanings

explanation.surface: A list of reptiles and boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of creatures and craft; the point is that serpent and snake mean the same, as do ship and vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Words sharing the same meaning, such as serpent and snake, are what the term names.

clue.text: Sort of Scotch valley

definitions.meaning: a single malt whisky distilled in Speyside
a glen, the valley of the River Livet in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: The whisky takes its name from the Scottish glen of the River Livet where it is distilled.

clue.text: Joint title-holder

definitions.meaning: a ... of beef is a large double sirloin roasting cut
a nobleman of the lowest rank of the peerage holds a title

explanation.definitionFit: A double sirloin roast bears this name, and so does a peer of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Ceremonial dues, say

definitions.note: used here as a noun, the prescribed forms of a ceremony

indicators.note: say signals that the word for dues is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: your dues are what you are entitled to, your rights

explanation.surface: Fees payable for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ceremonial' looks like an adjective describing the dues, but it is the noun: the set forms of a ritual. RIGHTS (dues) is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial, as a noun, is the body of prescribed observances at a religious or formal occasion.

clue.text: A stately home for a Cardinal X ?

definitions.meaning: the Prime Minister's official residence at Downing Street, the home of the head of state affairs
a cardinal number is a counting number, and X is the Roman numeral for it

explanation.definitionFit: The Downing Street residence is known by its door number, and the Roman X is that cardinal number.

clue.text: Matilda's initial soulful lie, embarrassing but smooth !

indicators.note: the initial of a name is its first letter, here of Matilda's
something embarrassing throws things into disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl's first heartfelt fib causes awkwardness, though she speaks smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: M is Matilda's 'initial'; 'embarrassing' jumbles SOULFUL LIE to give the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetly flowing voice or style is honeyed, sweet and even, without harshness.

clue.text: Air-lines with standing orders

parts.note: an air is a tune and lines are words, so a song whose words everyone must rise to their feet for

explanation.surface: Aviation companies with regular instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air-lines' suggests aviation firms; read it as a tune (air) with words (lines), sung while people are under orders to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's official song is sung at public occasions while everyone stands up for it.

clue.text: Disgraceful rise in number with debts

indicators.note: in means that the word for rise is placed inside the pieces that follow it

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the ground

explanation.surface: A shameful increase in the number of people owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' looks like an increase but is TOR, a hill; it goes 'in' NO plus IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being widely known for something bad is the same as being shameful or infamous.

clue.text: The Purser was surprised !

parts.note: not a ship's officer but someone who purses the lips, which is how a person blows a note of astonishment

explanation.surface: A ship's officer was taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purser' looks like the ship's officer; it means one who purses the lips, as people do when they blow a note in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the lips together and blowing a shrill note is a common way to show astonishment.

clue.text: He-he, extra rum it distributes-that's the stuff !

indicators.note: to distribute is to spread around, so the letters of the words before are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone giggling as they hand out extra rum, declaring it just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributes' rearranges HEHE, EXTRA, RUM and IT. 'Stuff' here means cloth: the answer is a tweed fabric of mixed colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and this is a speckled tweed of mingled colours like moorland.

clue.text: Put a bold face, say, on an insult

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase for a bold face is spoken aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a front is a show of boldness, as in putting on a front

explanation.surface: Advice to show courage when someone insults you.
explanation.walkthrough: To put on a front is to show a bold face; 'a front' said aloud gives the answer. 'Put' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An open slight or deliberate offence is a snub given to someone's face.

clue.text: Banter makes less of it

definitions.meaning: a follower of Banting, the Victorian slimming diet named after William Banting, someone trying to lose weight
something that brings down size or amount

explanation.walkthrough: 'Banter' looks like teasing talk; it is a slimmer on William Banting's diet, someone shedding weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieter loses weight, and anything that lowers an amount is one that lessens.

clue.text: Goods ejected from planes early in the day ?

parts.note: jets are aircraft, planes
a.m. denotes the morning hours

explanation.surface: Cargo dropped from aircraft in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures cargo thrown from aircraft; really JETS (planes) and AM (morning).
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo thrown overboard from a ship to lighten it is the legal term for goods jettisoned.

clue.text: Tone it down, put your foot down

definitions.meaning: to make something less forceful or emphatic
on a piano, pressing the left pedal mutes the sound

explanation.definitionFit: Playing down a subject is like muting a piano, done by pressing the left foot lever.

clue.text: Old Easter frolic, chaps !

indicators.note: to frolic is to romp about, so the letters of the next word move around

explanation.surface: Lads larking about at a bygone spring festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolic' looks like holiday fun; it rearranges CHAPS. Pasch is an old word for Easter or Passover.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word, from the Hebrew for Passover, names the spring Christian festival.

clue.text: Change colour again by means of VAT ?

definitions.text: Change colour again by means of VAT ?

parts.words: Change colour again by means of VAT ?
parts.note: VAT suggests the tax, but a vat is the tub in which cloth is soaked to colour it

explanation.surface: Changing the price label again because of the tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised VAT suggests value added tax; it is a dyer's vat, the tub cloth is soaked in to colour it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring a fabric afresh in a dyeing tub changes its shade a second time.

clue.text: Rugby's pride

parts.note: a pride is a group of big cats, and the touring British and Irish rugby side takes that animal as its name

explanation.surface: What a rugby nation is most proud of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' seems to mean self-respect; it is a group of big cats, the name of the British and Irish rugby touring side.
explanation.definitionFit: The touring British and Irish rugby union team is named after the big cats that live in prides.

clue.text: Outstanding feature of " Cyrano de Bergerac

definitions.text: Outstanding feature of " Cyrano de Bergerac

parts.words: Outstanding feature of " Cyrano de Bergerac
parts.note: outstanding means sticking out: the hero of Rostand's play is famous for an enormous nose

explanation.surface: The best thing about a famous French play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means projecting, not excellent: Cyrano's huge nose is his defining feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, prominent nose is the famous trait of Rostand's swordsman-poet.

clue.text: A number of course to knock up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: A certain number of strokes on a golf course to knock up.
explanation.walkthrough: RAP (knock) read 'up' in a down clue. Par is the standard score for a golf hole.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course each hole has a standard number of strokes a good player should need.

clue.text: Farm-worker in the depression

parts.note: not a labourer in hard economic times but one who works in a trench, digging drainage channels

explanation.surface: A farm labourer during the Great Depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the depression' suggests the 1930s slump; it is a trench, where this farm worker digs and clears drains.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm labourer who digs and maintains drainage trenches works down in those hollows.

clue.text: The rattle, sir, must be remedied

indicators.note: to be remedied is to be put right, so the letters before are re-set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone telling a gentleman that the noise must be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be remedied' rearranges SIR MUST. A sistrum is an ancient Egyptian rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Egyptian percussion instrument has metal rods that jingle when shaken.
